title: Shallow Equality Comparator (shallowEqual)
problemStatement: Implement `shallowEqual(objA, objB)` matching the exact comparator used by `React.memo` and `PureComponent`. Returns `true` if all own keys are shallowly equal using `Object.is`.
interviewTrap: Using `===` instead of `Object.is` causes `+0` and `-0` to match incorrectly and `NaN === NaN` to fail.

testCases.name: Returns true for objects with identical top-level properties
testCases.testFn: return shallowEqual({ a: 1, b: 'x' }, { a: 1, b: 'x' });

testCases.name: Returns false when nested object references differ
Handles NaN properly via Object.is

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: By default, when a parent component renders, all its child components re-render recursively regardless of whether their props changed. `React.memo` bails out only if all props are shallowly equal.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for Object & Prop Identity Comparison (Object.is).
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In JavaScript engines (e.g. V8), Object & Prop Identity Comparison (Object.is) is optimized via inline caches, heap contexts, and bytecode translation.
edgeCasesHandled: Using `===` instead of `Object.is` causes `+0` and `-0` to match incorrectly and `NaN === NaN` to fail.

verifiedRules: Adheres to ECMAScript runtime evaluation specifications.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How does shallowEqual differ from Object.is?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: `Object.is(a, b)` checks if two references are identical. `shallowEqual(objA, objB)` first checks `Object.is(objA, objB)`. If false, it verifies that both are non-null objects with the same number of keys, and checks that every key in `objA` passes `Object.is(objA[k], objB[k])` against `objB`. It does NOT recurse into nested objects.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests understanding of React.memo and PureComponent comparison mechanics.

realWorldUseCases.description: Skipping component re-renders when passed props are shallowly equal to previous props.

howToExplain.opening: shallowEqual compares objects at depth 1, checking reference identity for each top-level key without recursing into nested structures.
keyPoints: Checks Object.is on the root objects first.
Compares key count and checks Object.is on every top-level property.
O(K) comparison where K is top-level property count.
The default comparison function in React.memo and PureComponent.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Shallow equality provides fast O(1) bailouts for component memoization.
analogies: Checking passport covers: you check if two people hold matching blue US passports, without opening the pages to inspect travel stamps.

commonMistakes.mistake: Passing inline object literals <Component style={{ color: 'red' }} /> to a memoized component.
commonMistakes.why: A new object reference is created on every render, causing shallowEqual to fail every time.
commonMistakes.correct: Memoize objects with useMemo or extract them outside the component.

followUpDeepDive.question: Why does Object.is differ from === regarding NaN and -0?
followUpDeepDive.answer: `Object.is(NaN, NaN)` is `true` (whereas `NaN === NaN` is false). `Object.is(+0, -0)` is `false` (whereas `+0 === -0` is true). React uses `Object.is` for state change detection.
